items.title: Agent Anomaly Detection: Safeguarding agents across other clouds
items.content: Agent Anomaly Detection now monitors ADK agents running across AWS, Azure, or on-premises by analyzing their traces and logs in your Google Cloud project. By ingesting OpenTelemetry-formatted data through the Telemetry API, it evaluates full conversations for behavioral drift without needing access to the agent's underlying runtime. This enables security teams to detect risks like rogue behaviors, tool misuse, and resource exhaustion across multi-cloud environments.

items.title: Check what your AI agents do before they do it, with Semantic governance policies
items.content: Semantic governance policies enable developers to govern AI agents by evaluating every proposed tool call inline before execution. Operating via Agent Gateway, the policy engine checks each action against user intent and plain-language rules to prevent unauthorized data sharing and prompt injection attacks. Developers can easily attach natural-language constraints to their agents and monitor auditable verdicts through Cloud Logging.

items.title: How to handle user, connector, and agent auth in Gemini Enterprise with a custom UI
items.content: When building a custom enterprise UI on top of Gemini Enterprise's :streamAssist API, developers must manually implement three core authentication layers. These include authenticating users or workloads via Google Identity or Workforce/Workload Identity Federation, managing third-party 3-legged OAuth (3LO) for Federated Connectors through the Keystore, and configuring on-demand per-tool OAuth for custom ADK agents using Vertex AI Agent Engine and GCP Auth Manager.

items.title: Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Tunix and Gemma 4 on Google TPUs
items.content: This post walks developers through training a multi-turn, tool-using LLM agent using Tunix and Gemma 4 on Cloud TPUs. By leveraging agentic Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and asynchronous vLLM rollouts, the approach significantly improves complex reasoning and tool compliance in interactive environments.

items.title: Distributed LLM Training Across Metros: Streaming DiLoCo in MaxText
items.content: Streaming DiLoCo in MaxText enables developers to efficiently train large language models across geographically distributed TPU slices by streaming parameter fragments instead of synchronizing full models at every step. This approach slashes cross-slice communication volume by over 60× and eliminates network stalls, allowing seamless multi-datacenter scaling without degrading model convergence or quality.

items.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen: a faster model for general purpose robotics
items.content: Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen brings strong spatial and embodied reasoning capabilities to a fast, efficient model built specifically for robotics. To help developers put these capabilities to work, the new Robotics plugin for Google Antigravity transforms the platform into a comprehensive workbench supporting rapid hardware bring-up, MuJoCo simulation, and closed-loop control. Developers can leverage these tools to transition from an unboxed robot arm to a fully functional real-to-sim-to-real application in an afternoon using natural language prompts and day-one support in the google-genai SDKs.

items.title: TPU Model Design Considerations and Optimization Guide
items.content: The newly launched AI-Hypercomputer/tpu-codesign guide provides hardware-grounded design rules to help developers maximize performance on TPUs for LLMs and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) workloads. Key principles include aligning reduction and output dimensions to 256 for systolic arrays, adopting LatentMoE to compress routed token traffic, and mapping parallel axes directly onto physical links.
